diagnosis.what_happened: The extraction logic in restore_comprehensive_references.py relied on a naive character length heuristic (len(text) > 20) to extract valid bibliographic references. Consequently, long document subheadings were erroneously extracted.
diagnosis.behavior_caused_outcome: Because some subheadings contain more than 20 characters, they bypassed the filter and were erroneously appended to the reference list.
diagnosis.what_should_have_happened: The script should have validated standard bibliographic markers (e.g., publication year in parentheses, structured punctuation, or DOI patterns) before classifying a paragraph as a reference.
diagnosis.rationale_why: Bibliographic references follow strict structured formats (like APA 7). Relying solely on string length lacks the precision needed to differentiate between narrative text, long headings, and actual citations.

desired_behavior: Enforce structural bibliographic validation (e.g., regex for a four-digit year enclosed in parentheses or APA 7 formatting) for reference extraction. Explicitly filter out subheadings.
generalization: Never use pure string length as a heuristic for structural text classification tasks (like reference extraction); always validate structural markers or domain-specific patterns.
